expected_title: EyasSat-cubed: a Low-cost On-ramp for Nanosatellite Programs
abstract: A significant barrier to entry for universities and other organizations to build CubeSats or other small satellite systems is the learning curve of getting students and other untrained personnel to work safely with expensive, irreplaceable flight hardware. To address this challenge over a decade ago, the United States Air Force Academy Department Astronautics developed EyasSat. This low-cost, desktop satellite simulator system provides a unique, hands-on learning experience as a part of an integrated space systems engineering curriculum. EyasSat is an educational kit of representative spacecraft subsystems that can be assembled, integrated, and tested in the classroom with simple ground support equipment. Since its development, thousands of students have experienced EyasSat at dozens of universities, high schools, defense contractors, and military schoolhouses worldwide, as well as at NASA and ESA. User feedback from the community over the past decade and the 3 meteoric rise of CubeSat popularity has resulted in a complete redesign of EyasSat. EyasSat (EyasSat-cubed) is a more robust, flight-representative hardware and software design that conforms to the CubeSat standard to serve as a platform for space education and training for the next decade.
